articles.author: tara.garwood
articles.rawDescription:
The Great Miami Hurricane of 1926: 100 Years of Hurricane Forecasting and Research
September 21, 2026
Predicting extreme weather events and warning the public was much more difficult before we had satellites, aircraft reconnaissance, computer models, radio, television, and the internet. In this talk, we will discuss the Great Miami Hurricane of 1926 and its effects, our understanding of weather and the state of forecasting at the time, what we learned from this event, and how we have advanced in the following 100 years.

This presentation is part of the NOAA Heritage Week 2026 Speaker Series.
Heritage

articles.title: These tropical trees breathe at night to survive drought
articles.rawDescription: Some tropical trees have evolved a clever way to survive drought by taking in carbon dioxide at night, allowing them to keep their pores closed during the hot daytime and conserve water. By comparing three Clusia species, researchers discovered that this water-saving form of photosynthesis, known as CAM, did not arise through a single evolutionary change. Instead, ancient genome duplications followed by millions of years of genetic reshuffling produced strikingly different strategies, from strong CAM to stress-triggered and hybrid forms.
